fatal_errors: The intervention is only described as an unspecified thermal processing technique, so it is neither reproducible nor meaningfully testable.
The proposed grain-refinement and stable-particle mechanism does not match the relevant L12 ordering, jagged FCC/B2 phase-boundary evolution, planar slip, and crack-initiation mechanism.
The hypothesis misses the central non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response, including maximum degradation near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
Low-cycle fatigue is substituted for the relevant post-aging tensile ductility or toughness response without justification.
The cited evidence concerns a different refractory HEA tested hot rather than the post-exposure behavior of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1, and it does not support the proposed intervention or mechanism.

The proposed experiment lacks an untreated control, structural measurements, and comparisons across the embrittlement and recovery temperatures, so it cannot discriminate or falsify the claimed mechanism.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad problem of thermally induced mechanical degradation in an HEA and names an untreated alloy as a comparator, but it does not reconstruct the material, intervention, mechanism, or characteristic response. Its 500–700°C range only incidentally overlaps the relevant window, while the asserted 1–2 hour duration and fatigue loading are unsupported. It also fails to address retention of the original strength–ductility combination. A decisive test would compare identically prepared as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 samples aged below 550°C, near 600°C, near 750°C, and above 750°C, measure tensile ductility/toughness and strength, and use TEM or TKD to determine whether dislocation pile-ups and cracks originate at jagged FCC/B2 boundary tips as L12 ordering varies.
